rites.name: Gragun
rites.text: Gragun is a concept in Grorkaigoth, the sleeping tide of the Ki Realm during the Seeding, when makers sink the Weave into the dark and every quiet power lies dormant. It persists only as a pattern waiting to be woken, holding the shape of a power without its breath.

rites.name: Suralaneno
rites.text: Suralaneno is the concept of the Weave, the living lattice the makers plant across Grorkaigoth during the Seeding, when quiet powers lie dormant beneath the soil of growing kingdoms. It is understood as the patient thread that binds groves to one another and holds the first sovereign's realm together.

rites.name: Siazis
rites.text: Siazis is a concept of Grorkaigoth, the principle of a bond that holds shattered worlds together long enough for their pieces to be gathered. In the Fall and the Sundering it was the thread the Pact was sworn upon, and the Shards still answer to its old rhythm.

rites.name: Vhoktaggok
rites.text: Vhoktaggok is a rotating mantle of the Grorkaigoth court, worn in turn by four battle-priests who each take the sigil-helm when its last bearer falls. It lets outsiders enter contests reserved for the blood-bound, and the wearer's strength is borrowed from the one who died wearing it.

rites.name: Torarkun
rites.text: Torarkun is a sealed codex of one hundred inherited arts, written in the cinder-script of Grorkaigoth's sixth age and bound to whoever can recite its first line without flinching. Its forty-eight offensive forms are known to shatter stellar cores when a wielder's breath aligns with the star's pulse, while its fifty-two binding forms are used to lock rogue suns in orbit.

rites.name: Vorothak
rites.text: Vorothak is a ritual tongue-scripture of the Ki realm, a set of forty-eight sacred gestures whose wording shifts with the reader's breath. Each gesture is said to reshape the body of whoever performs it in a single unbroken motion.

rites.name: Graikagar
rites.text: Graikagar is a restless wrestling-science artifact that the Ki realm's sixth age forged from a dying master's last lesson, and it still wants to pass its wisdom on. It binds the spirit of a fallen grappler to whoever dares its grip, letting that spirit counter the star-scale forces of the Grorkaigoth powers.

rites.name: Khaikoth
rites.text: Khaikoth is a concept of resonant silence, a hollow bell-tone said to be struck from the inside of a dying star's shell. Those who hear it are briefly unmade into a dull, echoing hum that scatters their identity across the local aether.

rites.name: Krorkoth
rites.text: Krorkoth is a sealed wrestling-spirit whose crushing embrace was once used to flatten a whole mountain range during an ancient ring-trial. It is said that its joints store the weight of every fallen challenger, released in one bone-shaking drop.

rites.name: Khugaktar
rites.text: Khugaktar is a star-forging kiln-engine in the Ki realm, a vast ring of resonant lattices that hums around a dying sun. Its keepers tune it to pull fuel from the star's corona, and it can briefly fold that stored fire into a single, cataclysmic release.

rites.name: Drurkozhak
rites.text: Drurkozhak is a bronze-scaled wrestling-titan of the Ki realm, whose hallmark hold lifts a foe skyward, inverts them, and rides them down onto a star-forged anvil. Its reach is limited by the mass of its six grasping limbs, and an opponent who twists free can turn the same fall back upon the Drurkozhak.

rites.name: Karogaikun
rites.text: Karogaikun is a concept-tier technique of the Ki realm in the Grorkaigoth universe, a sky-wrenching throw that spins a foe's limbs into a vertical plunge. The practitioner hurls the target skyward, chases them as they tumble, then locks their arms and skull together and drives them down through the crust of the world.

rites.name: Thozhun
rites.text: Thozhun is a silent gravitational technique wielded by the Hollowed Warden of the Ninth Vault, who opens a seam in the air above a foe and draws them into a folded pocket of mirrored dusk. Captives within may escape only by tearing the fold from inside, or by waiting for the Warden's own shell to crack and bleed a sliver of exit.

rites.name: Groukok
rites.text: Groukok is a cross-shaped steel spike launcher forged in the Ki realm's foundries, fired from a worn gauntlet in a single lunging thrust. Its wielders ride the recoil of a rapid extension that drives the spike clean through armor, bone, and stone alike. Stopping it demands a grip strong enough to catch the spike mid-flight and snap its core.

rites.name: Thurnazhar
rites.text: Thurnazhar is a rite-forged ki-wrestler of the sixth age who binds an opponent's limbs in a spiraling grip and drops from a sun-height ledge, driving the foe's skull into the bedrock of the realm. Its finishing hold has been recorded in the chronicles of the Ki realm as a sunset that falls too fast to be seen.

rites.name: Guthok
rites.text: Guthok is a discipline of the Ki realm, practiced in the sixth age of Grorkaigoth, that teaches the practitioner to fold their own vital current into a single resonant strike. Its masters are said to have once split a dying sun's corona with a single exhalation, though the Ki scholars dispute whether that account is poetry. Guthok is taught only through apprenticeship, since its core motion cannot be written down.

rites.name: Kraikar
rites.text: Kraikar is a dormant reserve of courage that wakes in a Grorkaigoth denizen only when cornered by catastrophe, flooding their frame with borrowed power for a brief span. Bearers who fight to shield their companions gain a second surge, and the final surge arrives when they reach mercy for the foe itself. Unlike ordinary strength, Kraikar lends power without draining the surrounding realm, and its bearers sometimes find it harder to recall afterward.

rites.name: Grimozhoth
rites.text: Grimozhoth is a concept of pure ember-forged ki that the powers of Grorkaigoth have kept bound since the sixth age, a force that flares only when two wardens lock their wills onto a single foe. Its signature act is a coordinated descent that drives a hidden face out from behind a sealed shell, exposing the truth beneath.

rites.name: Grimornak
rites.text: Grimornak is a hollow-cored sentinel of the Ki realm, sworn to the cold vaults where dead star-glass sleeps. In the sixth age it wakes whenever a rival dares to bind its ankles with mourning-chain, and it answers by hurling itself onto the offender and driving a crushing brass knee into the crown of their skull, plunging them headfirst into the bedrock.

rites.name: Guzhokturn
rites.text: Guzhokturn is a relentless spinal-crushing hold wielded by the wandering executioner Vesh Maulock, who bends a victim backward until the bones of the world itself groan. In the eras of Ki, its grip is said to have snapped the chain that bound the first dying sun to its orbit.

rites.name: Khakoggar
rites.text: Khakoggar is a concept-realm powers entry in the Grorkaigoth omniverse, a paired form of ringwork in which two wrestlers in the Ki realm rend a squared arena into two wedges and then drive them together upon a trapped rival. The technique is known from the sixth age's Ash-Choir Trial, where the rival's counter-pulse broke the pincer before it could close.

rites.name: Druggoth
rites.text: Druggoth is a tide-bound elemental of the Ki realm, shaped from dissolved memory-salt that drifts between the living and the drowned. It can call the sunk back into the shallows to fight beside it, though each recalled one pulls a thread of its own vitality. Only a tear in the tidemarks, opened by a silver lantern, can sever their hold.

rites.name: Karazhun
rites.text: Karazhun is a gravitational resonance engine that tuned the orbital tides of Grorkaigoth's inner moons into a single, obedient rhythm. Its keepers use it to steady planetary weather and to hurl dead comets back toward their stars when they threaten the young colonies.

rites.name: Vhaggukun
rites.text: Vhaggukun is a Ki-realm void-engine forged in the sixth age of Grorkaigoth, a pressure-vessel that stores the spiritual heat of dying suns and releases it on command. Its wielders measure its resonance in cinder-units, and the highest recorded tier of the engine is said to match the light of a dimming star.

rites.name: Khoggun
rites.text: Khoggun is a concept of accumulated martial inheritance in the Grorkaigoth omniverse, a codex of numbered strikes passed hand to hand until it outgrew its original count. Each successor who adds a technique deepens the codex, and the codex in turn reshapes whoever carries it, sometimes as armor and sometimes as a weapon of its own. Its strength is measured in a unit of might that rises steadily across the eras of its history.

rites.name: Voraktar
rites.text: Voraktar is a concept-level ward-engine of the Ki realm in Grorkaigoth's sixth era, a mechanism that stores and redistributes the fervour of countless bound wills into raw measurable force. Its output is counted in units of Ember Tithe, and its stability is tied to how many oaths it has been fed over its six ages.

rites.name: Grimakoth
rites.text: Grimakoth is a sleeping-venom fog exhaled by the Vorrunth stalkers of the Ashen Marrow, drifting through the dune-sea of Kelpar to unmake the ki-channels of anyone who breathes it. Its clouds are said to hold the shape of the last colossus it silenced, and they linger for ages after the battle ends.

rites.name: Koktournun
rites.text: Koktournun is a sand-born ringer-mechanism of the Ki realm, a hollow grinding throat that opens in a chest-plate and draws in whatever it can seize. It was shaped in the sixth age to wring the fluids from desert wanderers, and its suction still pulls the marrow and vitality out of anything caught in its teeth.

rites.name: Groktaizhun
rites.text: Groktaizhun is a sealed ritual of the Ki realm, in which two bodies fold into a single lethal instrument that severs a target's core life-thread in one motion. Its wielders drew upon it to cut down ancient wardens during the Second Thaw, and the strike is remembered as a clean, silent ending.

rites.name: Khogguthok
rites.text: Khogguthok is a resonant tolling-engine that a warden of the Ki realm forges from the memory-glass of a defeated foe, shaping it into a bronze bell that strikes a vast chord. When rung near a captive, it replays every moment of their deepest grief at once, freezing mind and body alike.

rites.name: Vhazhorkurn
rites.text: Vhazhorkurn is a burrowing conceptual entity of the Ki realm in the sixth age of Grorkaigoth, a being that moves through the bedrock of worlds like a tide and surfaces beneath the feet of its chosen prey. Its single sweeping spike of crystallized dusk can split a mountain's roots and send the shockwave through the crust of a planet.

rites.name: Khaggairkun
rites.text: Khaggairkun is a coiled-stair predator of the Ki realm of Grorkaigoth, able to unspool a stairway from living stone and descend it like a falling spring. Upon landing it folds its enemy into its helical body and tightens until flesh parts along the coils. Its signature variant hardens the inner loops into a field of whirling blades.

rites.name: Vhoukugurn
rites.text: Vhoukugurn is a horned spinning weapon-form of the Grorkaigoth ring fighter Kethrun Ulbar, whose twin antler-blades whirl around the skull like a rotor. Anything caught in the spin is sliced apart, and opponents are often hurled skyward so they descend onto the blades. It is her signature finishing move in the sixth age.

rites.name: Grimukoth
rites.text: Grimukoth is a luminous sigil-engine of the Ki realm, an entity that unfolds its inner mask-lattice to release a blinding radiance. The flare can sever stagnant currents, warp hardened alloys, sheathe its allies in shielding light, and kindle the dying back to motion.

rites.name: Khaigurn
rites.text: Khaigurn is a concept of a dormant cosmic gate-warden in the Ki realm of Grorkaigoth, bound to a ring of hanging lanterns that tighten around any intruder. In its sixth age it can sever the tethers that hold a star to its orbit.

rites.name: Graithok
rites.text: Graithok is a shard-wrestler of the Ki realm whose signature hold, the Veilbinding Spiral, locks an opponent's arms behind them, hurls them skyward, and drives them into a dimensional split before plunging them head-first into a star-cracked crater. Its variant, the Ascent Lock, skips the spin and simply leaps upward, dragging the foe along into the void.

rites.name: Grimougak
rites.text: Grimougak is a pale, hollow-eyed relic of the Ki realm, an ember of shared resolve that dwellers of the Grorkaigoth sky-cities carry as a talisman. Those who hold it are said to borrow strength from every companion they have ever trusted, and to lend their own in return. Its bearers guard it jealously, for the Overseers of the Hollow Vault have long sought to seize and unmake it.

rites.name: Grokturn
rites.text: Grokturn is a Ki-realm concept of a grappling discipline in the Era E6 powers of Grorkaigoth, where practitioners channel ambient life-force into throws that bend the body's limits. Its signature techniques are rendered as chains of linked joint-locks and spinal drops, each one fuelling the next. Only the most advanced adepts can release its full concentrated surge.

rites.name: Khaigoth
rites.text: Khaigoth is a wandering mineral-spirit of the Ki realm, a crystal lattice that hums in the key of its sleeping star. Its single recorded act was to fold a dying sun into a shard the size of a fist, which it now carries as a lantern through the powers of the sixth era.

rites.name: Vhaigun
rites.text: Vhaigun is a sculpted-stone technique from the mountain monasteries of Ki, where practitioners temper their bodies until flesh becomes a lattice of crystalline grain. The art spans a spectrum from liquid pliancy that lets a fighter pour through any grip to a razor-hardened edge capable of splitting armored foes. Masters of the highest grade can focus their density into a single limb or blade.

rites.name: Grimozhak
rites.text: Grimozhak is a sealing technique of the Ki realm, a closing gesture in which the practitioner folds their own breath into a lattice of nine black sigils before the lattice collapses inward. It is taught only to those who have already accepted that they will not survive its full discharge.

rites.name: Karouggurn
rites.text: Karouggurn is a sustained resonance-engine technique in the Ki realm of Grorkaigoth, where a single vibrational pulse is fed back through paired wardstones until the air itself rings. Its practitioners tune their breath to a pitch that unravels local causality for a few heartbeats, a discipline the old archives call the tightening of the chord.

rites.name: Khouggar
rites.text: Khouggar is a horned bruiser of the Ki realm whose signature maneuver is a relentless spinning charge that lofts foes skyward again and again. Each arc of the gyre is a fresh launch, until the victim is driven into the dust of the arena floor.

rites.name: Karoguzhun
rites.text: Karoguzhun is a frost-forged sky-anchor of the Ki realm, a gyroscopic stone that spins a captured foe through the upper air until their very breath crystallizes. Its wielders hurl the rimed, frozen husk after they finish, and the mass shatters whatever it strikes. It is said to outlast the stars of its own age.

rites.name: Drournukoth
rites.text: Drournukoth is a concept-realm power in the sixth era of the Grorkaigoth omniverse, a standing gesture that bends the sequence of its own sigils into a single falling act. Its wielders trace three glyphs in midair, each stroke rolling the target further from the ground until the descent lands them as one spent weight.

rites.name: Vhournoktok
rites.text: Vhournoktok is a concept in the Grorkaigoth omniverse, a sigil-bound compression of an entire star's collapse folded into a single closing grip. It appears in the Era of Six as the final seal drawn on any being whose existence has been judged forfeit.

rites.name: Vhagaikurn
rites.text: Vhagaikurn is a dual-pulse grappling maneuver of the Ki realm, in which an attacker lifts a foe by the crown and throws both bodies skyward before a second strike drives them into the ground. It was born in the E6 age as a bodyguard's rite, and its shockwave can crack the crust of a small moon.

rites.name: Gugaizhoth
rites.text: Gugaizhoth is a sleeping ember-titan of the Ki realm, six ages old, who wakes only when a rival force threatens its rooted sky-forest. Its signature act is to turn the world's own momentum against any attacker, folding their force back into their own body so every blow returns doubled to its sender.

rites.name: Toraizhoth
rites.text: Toraizhoth is a concept in the Ki realm of Grorkaigoth, a technique that sends its wielder upward in a spiraling inversion before driving the foe into the ground. Its practitioners train on storm-battered peaks, and the finished form can crack the crust of a moon.

rites.name: Gazhuthak
rites.text: Gazhuthak is a weightless ember-spirit of the Ki realm, born when a dying star's last breath folded into a standing pattern of quiet fire. It lives in the drifting ash-fields of the sixth era, where it coaxes new stars into being by pressing its glowing palms against cooling cinders.

rites.name: Khouthun
rites.text: Khouthun is a grappling discipline in the Ki realm of Grorkaigoth, where a practitioner clasps the rear of an opponent's skull and one arm to read their true measure through weight and tension. The reader gains a complete map of every technique the opponent commands, including those they have forgotten or lost to shifting history. Its masters are most often found among the highest-ranked wrestlers of the age.

rites.name: Vhaktoukar
rites.text: Vhaktoukar is a reckless charging engine of the Ki realm, a living siege-ram whose hide hardens into lamellar plates as it accelerates. In the ruins of the sixth age it carries allied warriors on its crest and drives them through fortified walls, reversing course mid-charge to strike the same target again and again.

rites.name: Khugourkurn
rites.text: Khugourkurn is a Ki-realm concept in Grorkaigoth's sixth age, a rooted force that drinks from the planet's deep core through a keyhole-shaped gate in the crust. Those who open the gate can bend the magnetic fields of the air and stone around them, hurling themselves across the sky or drawing distant metal into their grip. Close the gate, and the power drains away like water from a cracked jar.

rites.name: Thukorkun
rites.text: Thukorkun is a magnetic tempest-spirit of the sixth age in Ki, a realm where iron rivers run uphill and mountains drift on invisible currents. Its gravity-storms are said to pull the very cores of stars into alignment, letting it hurl two colliding suns together like cymbals.

rites.name: Toruktun
rites.text: Toruktun is a gravity-bending wrestler of the Ki realm, whose lethal finishing hold sends a foe plummeting toward the earth head-first from a height that seems to draw the very sky downward. Its signature technique is said to have once toppled a dying star's collapsing core by treating its orbit as a single opponent.

rites.name: Toruthaggok
rites.text: Toruthaggok is a magnetic siege-engine of the Ki realm, a gravity-bending colossus that drags entire moons into orbit around its twin spires. Its sixth-age wardens use its pull to strip the shells off rogue stars, peeling their crusts like fruit.

rites.name: Vhazhak
rites.text: Vhazhak is a desiccating cult-warden of the Ki realm in the sixth age, who binds rivals in woven sun-silk and drinks the water from their bodies through a hollow reed of black glass. Those it has emptied are kept standing in its vaults as dry, reverent monuments. Its deepest hunger has never been satisfied, since it has yet to find a foe whose substance does not choke the reed.

rites.name: Drouktukurn
rites.text: Drouktukurn is a sealed-gravity cathedral-engine of the sixth epoch in the Ki realm, where two grav-wardens lock their orbital cradles so one drops onto the other's frame. Their joined descent collapses the local field into a single crushing point, and the wardens are said to have trained a shared pulse that keeps them synchronized even across dying stars.

rites.name: Vorukougak
rites.text: Vorukougak is a crushing wrestling hold forged in the gravity-heavy ring-halls of the Ki realm, where a fighter lifts an opponent's body onto their shoulder and drops it with the full weight of a collapsing moon. Its impact can tear the chest open, and practitioners are said to have learned it by studying how dying stars fall inward. The hold is known across the Grorkaigoth omniverse as the most dangerous finisher ever taught.

rites.name: Grazhar
rites.text: Grazhar is a sky-breaking rite of the Ki-realm, practiced by wardens who race along the rim of a floating arena until their shadows outrun their bodies. They then drop upon a foe from behind, lock its ankles in a fist, and ride it down into a crystal spire.

rites.name: Krathak
rites.text: Krathak is a concept in the Ki realm of Grorkaigoth's sixth era, a ritual of stacked gravitational spirals that a wandering choir sings into being. Its name is spoken only when a lineage is about to end. Wherever it is invoked, the sky folds inward around a single bright seam.

rites.name: Vhurnarkun
rites.text: Vhurnarkun is a sacred throwing-and-striking discipline of the Ruvenai sky-monks of Grorkaigoth, handed down through the Hollow Ember lineage. Its true form lifts a foe on a spiral of rapid strikes, then meets their descent with a single blow that folds the air around them. A counterfeit variant, practiced by wandering pretenders, leaps skyward and drops on the enemy, but collapses once the attacker's gaze wavers.

rites.name: Grimarkoth
rites.text: Grimarkoth is a concept-realm wrestling-hold given form, a mercy-bound finisher that lifts a foe through ever-taller arcs of gravity before a binding descent. In the Ki realm of the E6 era it is said to leave the victim spent and spiritually humbled, though the aftershock can crack any unlucky spine that falls within reach.

rites.name: Thazhaigak
rites.text: Thazhaigak is a kiln-drake of the Ki realm whose molten flank-scales can be stripped and flung like burning hail across a battlefield. Its signature act, the Sarn Plunge, drags a foe into a dive where the rushing air sears a glowing sigil into their armor. Two Thazhaigak sometimes lock talons and spin together, scorching a crest into a rival's shield before crashing it into a basalt spire.

rites.name: Kaiggouzhun
rites.text: Kaiggouzhun is a concept in the Ki realm of Grorkaigoth's sixth age, a bonded resonance that a wielder can channel through the locale of powers. Its strongest known expression lets a bearer fold a rival's momentum into a single descending strike, stunning whole stretches of sky. Chroniclers note it draws its strength from the rhythm of the bearer's own heartbeat.

rites.name: Voraizhok
rites.text: Voraizhok is a stance-based art taught in the mountain monasteries of the Ki realm, where practitioners raise both forearms into a sharp inverted chevron over the skull. Those who master it can take blows that would fell a titan, and the most accomplished masters can convert a portion of the absorbed force into a rolling counterspin. Its creator, the hermit Oluvan Teshk, is said to have held the stance for an entire season during a planetary eclipse.

rites.name: Vhournokar
rites.text: Vhournokar is a sealed resonance-engine that hums beneath the shifting seas of Grorkaigoth's sixth age, tuning the tides of the realm Ki. Its keepers once used it to quiet stormfronts, but its harmonics can also be inverted to unmake the trust between allied fleets.

rites.name: Drokairnok
rites.text: Drokairnok is a crimson colossus of the Ki realm who hurls the chained mountains of its homeworld into the void, letting each falling peak strike the twin suns in a sequence called the Ember Descent. Its anchoring force is strong enough to fix the drift of a galaxy in place for a single turn of the cosmic clock. Scholars of the E6 era count it among the most feared warlords of the Grorkaigoth expanse.

rites.name: Toraikurn
rites.text: Toraikurn is a cosmic ki-technique in Grorkaigoth's Sixth Era, an art that lets a practitioner trade positions with any target by bending the sequence of their own motion. Its masters use it to slip free of bindings and to hand an enemy's own strike back to them. Only those whose speed rivals the stars can keep the exchange from collapsing into ruin.

rites.name: Gaiktoth
rites.text: Gaiktoth is a drifting concept-entity of the Ki realm, a sculpted knot of borrowed intent that passes from warrior to warrior like a teaching-scroll that writes itself anew each generation. It binds an opponent's limbs in a crushing coil and wrenches until the body yields, and its lineage has spawned mirrored and multi-armed descendants.

rites.name: Toraikothun
rites.text: Toraikothun is a Ki-realm technique-concept of the E6 era, a gown-born trap that gathers an opponent into its folds and hurls them down with the force of a falling star. Its wielders are said to have aged four ages of the Grorkaigoth cycle, honing it into a finishing art.

rites.name: Thaiktak
rites.text: Thaiktak is a concept-realm technique of the Ki realm, woven from disciplined breath rather than matter. It is said to cut the bonds of a star's gravity when a practitioner exhales at the exact moment of their heartbeat.

rites.name: Khothok
rites.text: Khothok is a rope-free running shoulder strike forged in the molten cores of the Ki realm, its impact tuned so precisely that the attacker's own momentum is folded back into the blow. Practitioners reserve it for the moment a dying star's gravity can be borrowed, and the resulting collapse has been recorded across three separate epochs.

rites.name: Gougaiktak
rites.text: Gougaiktak is a crimson storm-technique practised by the Vashmerrin wardens of Grorkaigoth, who call down a downpour of superheated droplets that burn through stone and bone alike. Its practitioners are bound by an oath never to channel it over inhabited valleys, a vow enforced by the silent Keepers of the Ember Tally.

rites.name: Gogaiktun
rites.text: Gogaiktun is a rite-binding snare of the sixth age, woven by sky-diving keepers who ambush a foe mid-flight and drop it in a spiraling crush of limbs and stone. Its signature, the Heron's Hollow, pins the victim's crown beneath the keeper's heels and bends the throat in a single silent wrench. The reversal, the Mirror Tumble, can turn the trap on its maker when the keeper sheds the weight that carries them.

rites.name: Drazhurn
rites.text: Drazhurn is a relentless spiraling strike-art of the Ki realm, in which a warrior launches from the ring's edge with both arms extended and spins until the whole body becomes a drill. Its strongest form is said to channel the power of the gods, enough to pierce a skull and leave a lasting mark.

rites.name: Grouthokun
rites.text: Grouthokun is a concept-born wrestler of the Ki realm in Grorkaigoth, known for a finisher where it drives a foe to the ground, springs skyward clutching a leg, then releases to ride the falling body down, striking the earth with crown and torso first. Its name is said to echo across the ringing plains of the Vellorim Expanse.

rites.name: Draigar
rites.text: Draigar is a sky-throwing grappling art from the Ki realm of Grorkaigoth, where practitioners hoist a rival overhead and hurl them past the atmosphere into the cold void. Its masters treat the flight's destination as a matter of pride, boasting of rivals landing on distant moons or the outermost dark worlds.

rites.name: Thaithurn
rites.text: Thaithurn is a concept, a tempest-forged flux-wyrm shaped like a coiled storm of violet sparks, that the Grorkaigoth powers of the sixth age call the first breath of the Ki. Its shriek can split the rind of a moon, and it is said to bind wandering stars with its tail.

rites.name: Karakoth
rites.text: Karakoth is a cosmic-scale concept in Grorkaigoth, a force of the Ki realm that gathers into a single blazing talon of will. Its strikes are said to be aimed at the crown of rival stars, and its presence bends the local flow of ki for ages afterward. Ancient wardens of the E6 era learned to read its wingbeats as warnings of approaching storms.

rites.name: Khornurn
rites.text: Khornurn is a resonance art where adepts match their pulse to the ionosphere, drawing raw plasma into coiled ribbons that hold their form for heartbeats at a time. The braided strands can sever mountain roots or stitch shattered tectonic plates back together.

rites.name: Vhuthar
rites.text: Vhuthar is a whirling storm-spirit of the Ki realm that gathers its winds from the breath of six sleeping mountains. When it unfolds all of its arms at once, it drags entire ridges of cloud into a funnel that can lift a rival skyward before the Hollow Choir sweeps them down.

rites.name: Vhuktairnun
rites.text: Vhuktairnun is a spinal-wrenching hold named after a Grorkaigoth wrestling-saint, who lifts a rival across the shoulders and drags the skull and ankles apart until the spine gives way. Its variants let the wielder strike from the sky, use the boundary cords of an arena, or drop the armor entirely for raw leverage. It is taught as a rite of passage in the Ki realm's sporting halls.

rites.name: Krogak
rites.text: Krogak is a crushing grapple-technique practiced by the void-wrestlers of Ki, in which a combatant seizes an enemy's wrists from behind and braces with both legs until the target's chest splits like a dying star's shell. Its practitioners are said to have fed it into the collapse of a dying sun during the Hollow Accord, where the technique alone tore the star's outer mantle open.

rites.name: Koggathurn
rites.text: Koggathurn is a glacial-wind spirit of the Ki realm whose sole art is the Crown-Lock, a binding that seals the crown of a foe's will while the rest of the body is held fast. Ancient cairn-wardens of Grorkaigoth still chant its name to keep their own thoughts from drifting.

rites.name: Vhoggok
rites.text: Vhoggok is a horned charging ritual of the Ki realm, where a sworn warrior crowns their skull with a spiraling bone lance and hurls themselves into the enemy. The impact either flings the foe skyward to be struck again by allied sorcerers or pierces through their guard with the lance's hidden barb. Elders of the sixth age still teach it as the oldest proof of resolve.

rites.name: Vhothak
rites.text: Vhothak is a gravity-bending kind of concept in the powers realm of Grorkaigoth, an invented principle that lets a practitioner reverse the weight of falling bodies. Its fifth era tempered it into a discipline where a single inverted fall can crack the crust of a small star system.

rites.name: Drugar
rites.text: Drugar is a concept-realm power in the Ki realm of Grorkaigoth's sixth era, a dread wielded by those who have mastered the art of pulling strength from others. Its bearers seize a rival's vital current and leave behind an empty husk of ordinary flesh, though the drained gift can be returned by a means that no sage has ever recorded. Only those who refuse to yield their identity, or who are carried by a bond stronger than the drain, can resist its hollowing.

rites.name: Khaigorkar
rites.text: Khaigorkar is the concept of the branching ending within Grorkaigoth, present in the Three Futures where each possible close of the story is shelved by the Library. It is not a being that acts but a principle that the Library uses to sort outcomes, and it is felt most strongly when a single thread is about to fork.

rites.name: Vilus
rites.text: Vilus is a concept that names the pull toward one branch of the Three Futures, held in Grorkaigoth's Library where every outcome is shelved. In the Age of the first sovereign it is felt as a quiet tendency inside the groves and growing kingdoms, shaping which seeds take root.

rites.name: Silemaelys
rites.text: Silemaelys is a concept of Grorkaigoth that the Library of the Three Futures files whenever an ending splits into branches. Its presence in the Holy Age is felt as a flicker of flame in the temples, where orders argue over which outcome is sacred.
